# Overview

This report summarizes the spatial benchmarking analysis, including:

- Statistical tests (Wilcoxon + GLMM)
- Model diagnostics
- Log-fold change (LFC)
- Directional significance heatmaps

# Load Libraries block
```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(SpatialModelBenchmark)
library(tidyverse)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(ggpubr)
```

# Load parameters into objects
```{r}
counts_and_dens <- params$data
all_pvalues <- params$results
lfc_res <- params$lfc
shuffle_res <- params$shuffle
user_params <- params$user_params
glmm_models <- glmm_models
glmm_results <- params$glmm_results
```

cat("Number of samples:", nrow(counts_and_dens), "\n")
cat("Number of features:", ncol(counts_and_dens), "\n")

table(counts_and_dens$Group)

# **10. Directional Heatmap**


```{r, fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
# 1. Establish your color configurations
comps_elements <- sort(unique(c(pval_df$group1, pval_df$group2)))
shared_colors  <- setNames(
  viridisLite::viridis(length(comps_elements), option = "D"),
  comps_elements
)

# 2. Extract statistical model columns dynamically
test_cols <- grep("_pval_adj$", colnames(pval_df), value = TRUE)
model_names <- gsub("_pval_adj", "", test_cols)

# 3. FIX: Clean cell_type names safely using a regex pattern
# This clears both patterns ("_counts" and "dens") simultaneously across all rows
pval_df <- pval_df %>%
  mutate(cell_type = gsub("_counts$|dens$", "", cell_type))

# 4. Pull LFC structures
lfc_results <- params$lfc
write.csv(lfc_results$wilcox$lfc_grid, 'wilcox.csv')

# 5. Build an automated, model-agnostic LFC map list based on your data columns
dynamic_lfc_list <- lapply(model_names, function(mn) {
  if (mn == "wilcox") {
    return(lfc_results$wilcox$lfc_grid) # Density LFC for Wilcoxon
  } else {
    return(lfc_results$wilcox$lfc_grid)   # that was intentional to provide LFC direction based on density
  }
})
names(dynamic_lfc_list) <- model_names

# 6. Execute Heatmap Engine
pvalueHeatmap_directional(
  pvalue_df         = pval_df,
  lfc_list          = dynamic_lfc_list,
  cols              = test_cols,
  draw_heatmap      = TRUE,
  group_cols        = c("group1", "group2"),
  comparison_colors = shared_colors 
)
```
# Log Fold Change (LFC)
```{r}

library(dplyr)

# Standardize and add a tracking column to each source
glmm_lfc <- lfc_res$glmm$lfc_grid |> 
  dplyr::mutate(model_type = "glmm")

wilcox_lfc <- lfc_res$wilcox$lfc_grid |> 
  dplyr::mutate(model_type = "wilcox")

# Combine them into a single, master data frame
lfc_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(glmm_lfc, wilcox_lfc) |> 
  dplyr::rename(cell_type = Cell_Type)

head(lfc_df)

```

# **10b. Violin Plot Validation of Significant Results**

```{r, fig.height=5, fig.width=10, message=FALSE}


# --- 1. Extract significant cell types WITH comparison context ---
sig_results <- pval_df |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_any(
    dplyr::all_of(test_cols),
    ~ .x < 0.05
  )) |>
  dplyr::select(cell_type, group1, group2, dplyr::all_of(test_cols))

sig_cell_types <- unique(sig_results$cell_type)


# --- 2. Pivot raw data to long format for plotting ---
plot_data_all <- counts_and_dens |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      dplyr::all_of(params$count_cols),
      dplyr::all_of(params$dens_cols)
    ),
    names_to  = "raw_col",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Measure = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl(user_params$colGLMM,   raw_col, fixed = TRUE) ~ user_params$colGLMM,
      grepl(user_params$colWilcox, raw_col, fixed = TRUE) ~ user_params$colWilcox,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    cell_type = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl(user_params$colGLMM,   raw_col, fixed = TRUE) ~
        gsub(user_params$colGLMM,   "", raw_col, fixed = TRUE),
      grepl(user_params$colWilcox, raw_col, fixed = TRUE) ~
        gsub(user_params$colWilcox, "", raw_col, fixed = TRUE),
      TRUE ~ raw_col
    )
  )
  # No filter here — filtering happens per-comparison in the loop


# --- 3. Loop over each significant comparison ---
comparisons <- sig_results |>
  dplyr::distinct(group1, group2)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(comparisons))) {

  g1 <- comparisons$group1[i]
  g2 <- comparisons$group2[i]

  cat("\n--- Plotting comparison:", as.character(g1), "vs", as.character(g2), "---\n")

  sig_cts <- sig_results |>
    dplyr::filter(group1 == g1, group2 == g2) |>
    dplyr::pull(cell_type)

  label_df <- build_labels(
    pval_df   = pval_df,
    lfc_df    = lfc_df, 
    test_cols = test_cols,
    g1        = g1,
    g2        = g2
  )

  plot_data_comp <- plot_data_all |>
    dplyr::filter(cell_type %in% sig_cts)

   #render_violin_plot(
   #  plot_data    = plot_data_comp,
   #  label_df     = label_df,
    # user_params=user_params,
   #  measure_name = user_params$colGLMM,
   #  title        = paste("GLMM |", g1, "vs", g2),
    # color_map    = shared_colors
   #)

  render_violin_plot(
    plot_data    = plot_data_comp,
    label_df     = label_df,
     user_params=user_params,
    measure_name = user_params$colWilcox,
    title        = paste("Wilcox |", g1, "vs", g2),
    color_map    = shared_colors
  )
}

```

# 11. Model Diagnostics

Avaialble as separated pdf output
```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=10, message=T,eval = F}  
library(DHARMa)

if (!is.null(glmm_results)) {

  cat("## Model Diagnostics (DHARMa)\n\n")

  count_cols <- params$count_cols

  # Get all unique group comparisons from pval_df
  comparisons <- pval_df |>
    dplyr::distinct(group1, group2)

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(comparisons))) {

    g1 <- comparisons$group1[i]
    g2 <- comparisons$group2[i]

    cat("\n\n## Comparison:", as.character(g1), "vs", as.character(g2), "\n\n")

    # Subset glmm_results to this comparison if it's keyed by comparison
    # Adjust the key format below to match however glmm_results is named

   for (j in 1:length(glmm_results)){
  model_df <- glmm_results[[j]]

    simoutput_df <- model_df |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        across(
          all_of(count_cols),
          ~ purrr::map(.x, \(model) simulateResiduals(model))
        )
      )
    simoutput_df
    modelQC(
      model_df,
      count_cols,
      simoutput_df = simoutput_df,
      QQplots      = TRUE,
      AIC_BIC      = TRUE
    )
   }
  
  }

} else {

  cat("No GLMM models available — skipping QC.\n")

}

```

# **12. Shuffle Analysis Summary**

```{r, fig.height=10, fig.width=10, eval = T, message=FALSE}
if (!is.null(shuffle_res)) {

  # ----------------------------
  # Extract shuffled data
  # ----------------------------
  shuffled_df  <- shuffle_res$shuffled_df
  shuffle_names <- shuffle_res$shuffle_names

  count_cols <- params$count_cols
  dens_cols  <- params$dens_cols

  cell_type <- gsub(
    user_params$colWilcox,
    "",
    colnames(counts_and_dens)[grepl(user_params$colWilcox, colnames(counts_and_dens))]
  )

  # ----------------------------
  # Check shuffle quality
  # ----------------------------
  expected_cols <- c(
    paste0(cell_type, user_params$colGLMM),
    paste0(cell_type, user_params$colWilcox)
  )

  valid_cols <- intersect(expected_cols, colnames(shuffled_df))

  missing_cols <- setdiff(expected_cols, valid_cols)
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    message("Removed missing columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }

  shuffleSummaryStats(shuffled_df, shuffle_names, valid_cols)[1:5, 1:5]

  p <- checkShuffle(shuffled_df, c("Sample_id", "Group"), shuffle_names)
  print(p)


  # ==========================================================
  # 1. Wilcoxon tests
  # ==========================================================
  res_list <- list()
  for (shuffle_col in shuffle_names) {
    res_list[[shuffle_col]] <- testWilcox(
      shuffled_df,
      shuffle_col,
      paste0(cell_type, user_params$colWilcox),
      show_test_details = FALSE
    )
  }

  wilcox_res_shuffle <- res_list |>
    tibble::enframe(name = "columnID") |>
    tidyr::unnest(cols = c(value)) |>
    dplyr::rename_with(~ gsub(user_params$colWilcox, "", .x))


  # ==========================================================
  # 2. DYNAMIC GLMM tests (Model Agnostic Loop)
  # ==========================================================
  # This loops over whatever is inside glmm_models dynamically
  glmm_shuffle_results <- lapply(seq_along(glmm_models), function(m_idx) {
    
    current_model <- glmm_models[[m_idx]]
    model_res_list <- list()
    
    for (shuffle_col in shuffle_names) {
      model_res_list[[shuffle_col]] <- testGLMM(
        shuffled_df,
        shuffle_col,
        add_formula_terms = current_model$formula,
        cols              = count_cols,
        family            = eval(parse(text = current_model$family)),
        show_test_details = FALSE
      )
    }
    
    # Process, unnest, and harmonize column headers immediately
    model_res_list |>
      tibble::enframe(name = "columnID") |>
      tidyr::unnest(cols = c(value)) |>
      dplyr::rename_with(~ gsub(user_params$colGLMM, "", .x))
  })
  
  # Assign a predictable list name string based on the model's family name
  model_names_clean <- sapply(glmm_models, function(m) m$family)
  names(glmm_shuffle_results) <- model_names_clean


  # ==========================================================
  # 3. Combine all p-values dynamically
  # ==========================================================
  # Combine Wilcoxon with our dynamically populated list of GLMM outputs
  master_p_list <- c(list(wilcox = wilcox_res_shuffle), glmm_shuffle_results)
  
  all_pvalues <- tibble::enframe(master_p_list) |>
    tidyr::unnest(cols = c(value)) |>
    getPvalues(cols = cell_type) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from  = name,
      values_from = dplyr::all_of(cell_type)
    )


  # ==========================================================
  # 4. Count significant values
  # ==========================================================
  sigcounts <- countSignificant(
    all_pvalues,
    grouping      = c("group1", "group2"),
    sig_id_format = "string"
  )

# ==========================================================
  # 5. Reshape for heatmap dynamically
  # ==========================================================
  df_long <- sigcounts %>%
    dplyr::select(group1, group2, dplyr::ends_with(".sig_counts")) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols          = dplyr::ends_with(".sig_counts"),
      names_to      = c("cell_type", ".value"),
      names_pattern = "^(.*)_(.*)\\.sig_counts$"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::relocate(cell_type, group1, group2) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(cell_type))

  # Identify what models exist as columns in df_long (excluding metadata cols)
  model_cols <- setdiff(colnames(df_long), c("cell_type", "group1", "group2"))


  # ==========================================================
  # 6. Final heatmap (With Explicit Column Routing)
  # ==========================================================
  sigcountHeatmap(
    sigcount_df     = tibble::as_tibble(df_long),
    n               = length(shuffle_names),
    cols            = model_cols, # FIX: Forces the function to read these columns directly
    row_name_col    = "cell_type",
    column_title    = "Random shuffle\nunadjusted p-values",
    column_title_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 16, fontface = "bold"),
    draw_heatmap    = TRUE,
    show_row_names  = TRUE
  )
} else {
  cat("No shuffle results available.\n")
}
```
